source_selection: Klich and von Delft-Schoeller supply the finite trace and constructive bosonization dependencies. Group-particle sources and NIST 20.5 were inspected as locators/comparators; no new nonabelian claim is made.
novelty: No novelty acceptance or exhaustive search. The trace identity, constructive bosonization and compact charging model are established; the explicit regulator-uniform bound and finite-reservoir certificate serve this matching decision.

development_failures.reason: An assumed fivefold decrease of the finite-volume error failed because the selected volume values already had volume corrections below the ultraviolet truncation floor.
development_failures.resolution: Added smaller optical circles, assessed the refined UV/grid limit against a stated absolute tolerance, and added 24 independent finite-circle lattice comparisons. No Hamiltonian or analytic bound changed.

accepted_scope: The full paired fermion spectrum with radial kinetic energies and total electric charging obeys exp(-x/2)<=b/b_free<=exp(x/4)/cosh(x/2).
The bound survives physical spatial localization; a finite-reservoir certificate derives the U(1) rotor midpoint in the optical-volume limit.
The finite-circle charge lattice gives an independent bosonized midpoint formula without adding an independent rotor.
limitations: The actual radial Coulomb kernel is not merely a total-charge square.
A screened inertia and the same explicit fermions cannot be combined without matching.
The angular sector, evolving state, stress and geometry are not computed.
The infinite-reservoir compact factor replaces the Gaussian zero mode; it is not an extra independent rotor.
decision: Use the uniform electric comparison and exact charge-lattice formula for initial-state matching. Next retain the full radial Gauss kernel and Wilson dressing; do not substitute screened inertia into a second copy of its fermions.
remaining_todo: Match the full radial electric Hamiltonian and dressed operator, with one compact mode and one oscillator subtraction.
Include joint angular and massive sectors and derive the driven two-time covariance/stress with evolving geometry.
Establish preparation, fluctuations, sufficient general stability and finite-energy transport.
